<ExternalIntegrationHeader integration={{"name":"Beem Energy","description":"Track your Beem solar kits (BeemBox, Beem On): production, history and savings.","owner":"Terdious","owner_avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/35010958?v=4","repo_url":"https://github.com/Terdious/gladys-beem-energy","cover_url":"https://integration-store-storage.gladysassistant.com/covers/Terdious--gladys-beem-energy.png","type":"device","version":"1.3.0","gladys_version":">=5.1.0","stars":0,"pushed_at":"2026-10-23T07:45:14Z"}} />

Track your **Beem solar kits** (BeemBox of the 300 W kits, Beem On of the 500 W
kits) in Gladys Assistant: live solar power, production of the day, the month,
the year and since the start, Wi-Fi signal of each box, savings and payback
estimate, and alerts when a box produces less than the others.

The integration reads the **Beem cloud**, with the account of the Beem
application: Beem boxes offer no local access.

## Requirements

- A **Beem account**, with your boxes already installed and visible in the Beem
  application.
- Gladys Assistant **5.1 or later**.

## Features

Every box of the account becomes a Gladys device, with:

| Feature                  | Category / type                                 | Unit |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- | ---- |
| Solar power              | `energy-production-sensor` / `power`            | W    |
| Solar production (index) | `energy-production-sensor` / `index`            | kWh  |
| Production today         | `energy-production-sensor` / `daily-production` | kWh  |
| Wi-Fi signal             | `signal` / `integer`                            | %    |

- **Every box in one request**: the Beem cloud answers for all the boxes of the
  account at once, read every two minutes by default (one minute at least: the
  cloud refreshes a box about once a minute).
- **A box asleep at night** (powered by its panels, it switches off at dusk)
  shows 0 W instead of its last power, as soon as its last report is older than
  15 minutes.
- **The production index** is the feature Gladys' **energy monitoring** turns
  into thirty-minute production. The Beem cloud only gives the production of the
  day and of the month: the integration computes its own index from the month
  total, and asks for the final total of the previous month on a month change.
  Nothing is lost at midnight, nor during a container downtime: the next reading
  catches up the missed production.
- **History**: at startup, the integration asks the Beem cloud for the
  production of the past months (24 by default, one request every few seconds,
  once per month: a past month never changes), then of the past days (hourly
  history, one week per request; when the cloud is slow to answer, the backfill
  resumes on its own an hour later, without a restart nor a click). The year,
  lifetime, savings and payback
  figures and the browsing of the widgets start there.
- The transport badge reads **cloud** for a box present in the cloud summary,
  **unreachable** for a box missing from it.

### Linking the production to the energy monitoring

In **Integrations → Energy monitoring**, add the **Solar production (index)**
feature of each box: Gladys derives the thirty-minute production and shows it in
its energy dashboards, next to your consumption.

## Configuration

| Field                      | Role                                                                 |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| E-mail, Password           | The account of the Beem application (the password is never logged).  |
| Refresh interval           | Seconds between two reads of the cloud (60 to 3600, 120 by default). |
| Months of history          | Months fetched at startup (0 to 120, 24 by default, 0 disables).     |
| Feature names language     | Language of the feature names of new boxes (English, French).        |
| Timezone                   | Days and months of the Beem cloud, off-peak hours, daily report.     |
| Tariff, prices…            | The savings estimate (see below).                                    |
| Underperformance threshold | The alerts (see below).                                              |

The **Test the connection** button signs in to the cloud and lists the boxes
found.

## Dashboard widgets

The card title is the name of the widget; give a **title** in its settings to
show another one (a box always shows its name).

Four widgets, added from **Dashboard → Edit → Add a widget**:

- **Beem box**: one box, over the period chosen. On the current day: **power
  curve** (5-minute averages) next to the **expected** curve (what the box
  would produce at the same yield as the other boxes, per kWp), live power,
  production of the day, **yield** of the day (kWh per installed kWp, comparable
  between a 300 W and a 500 W kit), time of the last report ("asleep" at
  night), Wi-Fi signal (dBm and %), **cuts of the day** (the moments of 5
  minutes or more the box produced nothing while the others produced, with the
  time of the last one), yield **against the other boxes** (in % of the median,
  or the underperformance alert), share of the peak power, month, panels (count,
  power, orientation in words: `SE -30°` = 30° to the east from the south, and
  tilt `∠30°`), yesterday, the year and the total. On another period: the curve
  (or the production bars) of the box against the expected one, its
  production, its peak power or best day, its yield and its place against the
  other boxes.
- **Solar installation**: the whole installation, **single-phase** (the boxes
  chosen, or all of them) or **three-phase**: assign the boxes of each phase
  (L1, L2, L3) in the widget settings. Periods: **12 hours** and **day** (power
  curve, one curve per phase in three-phase), **week** and **month** (production
  per day), **year** (production per month). On the current day: power, day,
  month, year, share of the peak power, one row per phase (power · production of
  the day), the **phase balance** (in warning past the threshold set, 500 W by
  default), the silent or low-yield boxes. On another period: production, peak
  power or average per day, best day, yield per kWp and the share of each phase.
  The assignment mistakes (a box in two phases, or in none) always show.
- **Solar savings**: savings per **month** (bars per day), per **year** (per
  month) or over **all the years**; savings and production of the period,
  **payback** gauge and date, total since the start, value of one solar kWh,
  self-consumed and exported shares of the period, CO2 avoided.
- **Production history**: production per **month** (bars per day), per **year**
  (per month) or over **all the years**; production, average and best day /
  month / year of the period, comparison with **the same period one year
  before** (same days or months), ranking of the boxes over the period (with
  their yield per kWp). The **Default period** setting picks the period shown
  first.

### Changing the period and browsing

Like on the charts of Gladys, the Box, Installation, Savings and History widgets
have their buttons:

- **Period** (the name of the period shown): opens a form with the periods of
  the widget and an optional **Go to the date** field. Empty, it goes back to
  the current period; filled, it shows the period holding that date. Gladys has
  no calendar in these forms: type the date, e.g. `05/09/2025`, `05/09` (the
  last 5 September), `09/2025`, `Sept 2025`, `September` or `2025`. A date to
  come shows the current period, a date not understood is said.
- **Previous** / **Next**: steps back or forward by one period (12 hours, day,
  week, month, year), from the date chosen too. Previous shows only when there
  is data before, Next once stepped back.

Box and Installation: **12 hours** and **Day** (power curve), **Week** and
**Month** (production per day), **Year** (per month). Savings and History:
**Month**, **Year** and **All years**.

The period shows in the chart title. It is kept per widget (per settings) while
the integration runs: two dashboards showing the same widget with the same
settings share their period, and a restart goes back to the default period. On a
Gladys older than 5.2, the Period button simply goes to the next period.

> Data: the fine curves (5-minute averages) are kept **14 days**. Before them,
> the past days have an **hourly curve** (titled "Hourly power"), from the
> hourly history of the Beem application fetched at startup (up to 400 days,
> one week per request), like the **daily** production; the **Diagnose the
> boxes** action tells how many days each box has. The months come from the
> monthly history.

### Example: 3 phases, 6 boxes

For 3 BeemBox (3 × 300 W kits each) and 3 Beem On (2 × 500 W kits each), one
BeemBox and one Beem On per phase: add the **Solar installation** widget, choose
**Three-phase**, then put in **Phase L1 boxes** the BeemBox and the Beem On of
L1, and so on. Each phase shows 1.9 kWp; the installation 5.7 kWp.

## Savings (estimate)

A plug-and-play kit has no grid meter: nothing tells which part of the
production the home consumed and which part went to the grid. The estimate
therefore rests on your figures:

> value of 1 kWh produced = self-consumption rate × solar price
>
> - (1 − rate) × resale price (0 without a resale contract: the surplus of a
>   kit without contract is given to the grid)

- **Tariff**: _Base_ (one price) or _Peak / off-peak_ (two prices and the
  off-peak ranges, e.g. `22:00-06:00` or `02:00-07:00,13:00-16:00`). With peak /
  off-peak, the **solar price** is weighted by when the panels produce: the
  curve measured over the last two days, or a standard daylight curve at first.
  Off-peak hours at night give a solar price close to the peak price; off-peak
  hours in the early afternoon lower it.
- **Self-consumption rate**: 100 % by default, realistic for a kit sized on the
  base load of the home. Lower it if your meter often shows an injection.
- **Resale**: if you have a contract selling the surplus, tick the box and give
  the price.
- **Cost of the installation**: what you paid for the kits (and their
  installation). The widget then shows the share paid back and the payback date,
  at the pace of the last 12 complete months.
- **CO2 avoided**: the carbon intensity of the grid electricity your production
  replaces (50 g per kWh by default, the order of magnitude of the French mix; 0
  hides the figure).

The savings are computed from the energy and the current tariff: a price change
applies to the past too. It is an estimate, not an invoice.

## Alerts and scenes

### Box underperforming

The boxes are compared with each other, size for size (production per installed
kWp):

- **Silent**: a box producing nothing for 30 minutes while the others produce
  (micro-inverter off, Wi-Fi lost, breaker tripped…).
- **Low yield**: from 14:00, a box whose yield of the day is below the
  **underperformance threshold** (60 % by default) of the median yield of the
  boxes, on a day bright enough to compare (0.5 kWh/kWp at least). If your boxes
  have very different orientations, lower the threshold; 0 disables the
  detection.

The alert shows on the widgets and fires the **Box underperforming** scene
trigger (filters: the box, the reason), once per box and per day. Variables:
`device_name`, `reason` (`silent` or `low_yield`), `ratio` (% of the yield of
the others), `today_kwh`.

### Daily production report

The **Daily production report** trigger fires once a day, when the solar day is
over (every box at 0 W for 30 minutes after 16:00, or at 22:00 at the latest).
Variables: `today_kwh`, `month_kwh`, `yield_kwh_per_kwp`, `savings`, `co2_kg`,
`best_box`, `best_box_kwh`. For instance, a message: "☀️ Production today:
\{\{triggerEvent.data.today_kwh\}\} kWh, \{\{triggerEvent.data.savings\}\} € saved".

### Get the solar production

The **Get the solar production** scene action returns the current figures of a
box, or of the whole installation when no box is chosen: `power_w`,
`today_kwh`, `month_kwh`, `year_kwh`, `load_percent` (share of the peak power),
`savings_today`, `savings_month`. For instance, a condition "if `power_w` >
1500" to start the dishwasher when the sun shines.

## Updating the integration

**Installed from the catalog** (the usual case): when a new version is out, the
integration shows an **"Update available"** badge and its **Supervision** tab
offers the version, with a link to its notes. Click **Update**: Gladys pulls the
new image and the new manifest. Your configuration, your devices and the history
(in `/data`) are kept.

**Installed in developer mode** (manifest pasted by hand): **"Force update"**
only pulls the image again; paste the up-to-date manifest again to get the new
fields.

## Troubleshooting

- **"The Beem cloud refused the e-mail or the password"**: use the credentials
  of the Beem application (not those of the online shop).
- **"Beem API rate limit reached"**: the Beem cloud blocks an account that signs
  in too often. The integration keeps its token for an hour and, after a refusal,
  waits 20 minutes before trying again. Avoid connecting the same account to
  several tools at once (Home Assistant, scripts…), or raise the refresh
  interval.
- **A box is unreachable**: it is missing from the cloud summary. Check that it
  shows in the Beem application.
- **No history**: run the **Reload the history** action (for instance after
  adding a box to the account).

### Diagnostic

The **Diagnose the boxes** action shows, for each box, what the cloud reports
right now (power, day, month, signal, last report) and what the integration
keeps (index, months of history). Attach it to an issue: it holds no e-mail, no
password and no token.

## Credits

The Beem cloud has no public API: the addresses and fields used were documented
by the community, notably the Home Assistant integration
[CharlesP44/Beem_Energy](https://github.com/CharlesP44/Beem_Energy) (MIT
License). The code of this integration is original.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Beem Energy asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Beem account | `section` | No | Sign in with the e-mail and password of the Beem application. The integration reads every solar box of the account through the Beem cloud (no local access exists). |
| E-mail | `string` | Yes |  |
| Password | `secret` | Yes |  |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the Beem cloud is read, in seconds (one minute minimum: the cloud refreshes a box about once a minute and limits the accounts that insist). |
| Months of history | `number` | No | Monthly production fetched from the Beem cloud at startup (year, lifetime, savings and payback). 0 disables it. |
| Language of the feature names | `select` | No | Applied to the boxes discovered from now on. |
| Timezone | `string` | No | IANA name: the days and months of the Beem cloud, the off-peak hours and the daily report follow it. |
| Savings estimate | `section` | No | Without a grid meter, the savings are an estimate: the production times the price of the electricity it saves you from buying, plus the resale of the surplus if you have a contract. Leave the mode on None to hide them. |
| Electricity tariff | `select` | No |  |
| Base price (per kWh) | `number` | No |  |
| Peak price (per kWh) | `number` | No |  |
| Off-peak price (per kWh) | `number` | No |  |
| Off-peak hours | `string` | No | HH:MM-HH:MM ranges separated by commas, in the timezone above. |
| Self-consumption rate (%) | `number` | No | Share of the production your home consumes at once. A kit sized for the base load is close to 100 %; lower it if the meter often shows an injection. |
| I sell my surplus | `boolean` | No | Off: the surplus is given to the grid (the usual case of a plug-and-play kit). |
| Resale price (per kWh) | `number` | No |  |
| Cost of the installation | `number` | No | What you paid for the kits (and their installation): the savings widget shows the payback. |
| CO2 avoided (g per kWh) | `number` | No | Carbon intensity of the grid electricity your production replaces. 0 hides the figure. |
| Alerts | `section` | No | The boxes of the installation are compared with each other (production per kWp installed): a box silent while the others produce, or far below them, is flagged on the dashboard and fires the "Box underperforming" scene trigger. |
| Underperformance threshold (%) | `number` | No | A box is flagged below this share of the median yield of the boxes. 0 disables the detection. |

## How to install Beem Energy in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Beem Energy appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/terdious/gladys-beem-energy:1.3.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/Terdious/gladys-beem-energy](https://github.com/Terdious/gladys-beem-energy).

Beem Energy requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Beem Energy is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [Terdious](https://github.com/Terdious), not by the Gladys core team.
